grades.quote: attempts to perform operations not permitted by the current privilege mode will cause an exception to be raised. These exceptions will normally cause traps into an underlying execution environment.
grades.reason: RISC-V passage says operations not permitted by the current privilege mode raise an exception that normally traps to the execution environment. This covers the general exception behavior. It doesn't name a specific cause such as illegal-instruction, and it doesn't focus on privileged instructions in U-mode.

grades.quote: PLV0 is the privilege level with the highest privilege and is the only privilege level that can use privileged instructions and access all privileged resources
grades.reason: LoongArch passage gives the execution rule: only PLV0 can execute privileged instructions, and PLV1-PLV3 (including user level PLV3) cannot. It doesn't state which exception is raised.

grades.quote: any attempt to perform hardware-level I/O or change memory accessibility interrupts the process’s execution and jumps to a handler in the operating system
grades.reason: Generic OS textbook passage. Kernel mode can execute any instruction, while a user-mode attempt at privileged operations (I/O, changing memory accessibility) traps to an OS handler. It is useful conceptually but not tied to a specific ISA or to the exact exception.

grades.quote: the execution of `RDTIME` instructions at the PLV1/PLV2/PLV3 level can be prohibited, or will trigger the **I** nstruction **P** rivilege error **E** xception (IPE)
grades.reason: LoongArch passage is about disabling the non-privileged RDTIME instruction at PLV1-3. It names the Instruction Privilege error Exception (IPE) raised in that case. It doesn't describe privileged instructions executed in user mode, so it only helps a little.
